title: Minimum Equal Sum of Two Arrays After Replacing Zeros
summary: Given two arrays of positive integers, replace all zeros in both with positive integers to make their sums equal.
statement: Given two arrays of positive integers, replace all zeros in both with positive integers to make their sums equal. Return the smallest possible equal sum, or -1 if impossible.
constraints: Both arrays are nonempty and contain nonnegative integers.
Replace every zero with a strictly positive integer so the final sums are equal.
Return the smallest possible common sum, or -1 if equality is impossible.
hints: Replacing each zero by one gives an array’s minimum attainable final sum.
The common sum must be the larger minimum; the lower side can reach it only if that side contains a zero.
Compute both minima, reject when the smaller fixed array cannot grow, otherwise return their maximum.
Any array with a zero can add arbitrary extra positive amount to one replacement, while an array without zeros has a fixed sum, proving both feasibility and minimality.
editorial: Any array with a zero can add arbitrary extra positive amount to one replacement, while an array without zeros has a fixed sum, proving both feasibility and minimality.

tests.explanation: Replacing zeros by positive values can make both sums twelve, the larger minimum.
The first array’s minimum is six, but the fixed second sum is five, so equality is impossible.
